paper.title_en: Self-gravitating Lee-Huang-Yang fluids as dark matter halos
paper.abstract_en: We propose a model of dark matter halos based on a self-gravitating Bose fluid whose effective equation of state is dominated by Lee-Huang-Yang quantum fluctuations. The model is governed by coupled generalized Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson equations, which incorporate quantum pressure, Lee-Huang-Yang-induced repulsion, and gravitational attraction. By retaining the full quantum pressure, we examine the halo structure from its central region to its asymptotic regime. We first derive the Jeans dispersion relation and analyze how the Lee-Huang-Yang fluctuations alter the gravitational instability criterion and the associated characteristic length and mass scales. We then obtain analytical expressions for the central and large-radius behaviors of the equilibrium solutions. To verify the validity and the performance of the model, we fit the model-predicted curves with a sample of 20 galaxies from the SPARC database and compare the results with those obtained from Navarro-Frenk-White, standard Bose-Einstein condensate, and quantum-droplet dark matter models. We find that the pure-LHY model reproduces a broad range of observed galactic kinematics, yielding reduced $χ^2$ values and a lower sample average compared to the aforementioned models. These results indicate that the combined effects of quantum pressure, LHY quantum fluctuations and the self-gravity provide additional flexibility in describing both the central and extended outer regions of galactic halos. We also discuss the implications of the inferred halo parameters and emphasize their dependence on the assumed effective equation of state and its microscopic interpretation. The pure-LHY model constitutes an ideal platform for exploring the role of quantum-fluctuation-induced interaction in the formation and structure of dark matter halos.
